create_provider.note: metadataXml is a proto bytes field — value MUST be base64-encoded. Use metadataUrl (string) as alternative.

oidc_jwt.description: Many UserInfo, introspection, ID token, and access token claims are only returned when the corresponding scopes are requested or configured.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag missing claims as identity or authorization bugs unless the relevant scope was requested.

oidc_jwt.description: User metadata claim values are base64 encoded in tokens and UserInfo responses.
oidc_jwt.note: Raw/plaintext comparisons will produce false mismatches.

oidc_jwt.description: The UserInfo endpoint accepts the access token of the user, not a client token.
oidc_jwt.note: 401 on UserInfo with machine/client tokens is by design.

oidc_jwt.description: Reserved organization scopes enforce organization membership and may fail authentication if the user is not a member or the organization does not exist.
oidc_jwt.note: Cross-org failures under these scopes are expected behavior, not authorization bugs.

oidc_jwt.description: Introspection returns active=true only if the token is active and the requesting client is part of the token audience.
oidc_jwt.note: An inactive introspection result can reflect wrong client context rather than token invalidity.

oidc_jwt.description: Token exchange supports only the documented token-type combinations; some subject_token_type and requested_token_type values are explicitly not allowed.
oidc_jwt.note: Rejection of unsupported token-type combinations is by design and should not be reported as a security issue.

oidc_jwt.description: Token exchange rejects scopes that exceed the scope granted by the resource owner with invalid_scope.
UserInfo and introspection only return many user claims when the corresponding scopes were requested.
oidc_jwt.note: Missing email/profile/phone/address/metadata/resource-owner claims without scopes is expected and should not be treated as claim stripping or identity confusion.

oidc_jwt.description: Access tokens include multiple audience values by default: all client IDs and the project ID.
oidc_jwt.note: A token having more than one audience is normal in ZITADEL and should not be flagged as overbroad unless it exceeds documented defaults or requested audience-expansion scopes.

oidc_jwt.description: Refresh token requests may specify scope only as a subset of the original authorization request; omitted scope reuses the original scope.
oidc_jwt.note: Rejection of broader refresh scopes is expected behavior, not a token-exchange or authorization-binding bug.

oidc_jwt.description: Introspection returns active information only when the requesting client is part of the token audience.
oidc_jwt.note: An inactive introspection result can reflect client-audience mismatch rather than token invalidity or revocation.

oidc_jwt.description: The urn:zitadel:iam:user:metadata claim contains base64-encoded values.
oidc_jwt.note: Comparisons against metadata must decode values first; encoded output is expected.

oidc_jwt.description: The token endpoint requires redirect_uri to exactly match the authorization request redirect_uri for authorization_code exchange.
oidc_jwt.note: redirect_uri mismatch failures are expected and should not be treated as flow confusion bugs.

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I2 freshness tests on JWT profile grant and token exchange, the fuzzer MUST include a control request using a valid token/assertion alongside the attack request. Use exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} and iat={{now_epoch}} for JWT-based controls. Without a control, LOGIN_FAILED or invalid_grant cannot be distinguished from broken client authentication or malformed request setup.
oidc_jwt.source: OpenID token endpoint docs and JWT/private_key_jwt claim requirements

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I1 proof-integrity tests against /oauth/v2/token using JWT profile grant, the JWT assertion MUST be signed and include a kid header identifying the downloaded key. ZITADEL documents RS256-signed JWTs with kid and does not document alg=none support; alg=none and attacker-signed assertions should be tested as rejection cases only.

For JWT assertions used either as authorization grants or private_key_jwt client authentication, aud MUST include ZITADEL's issuing domain (https://${CUSTOM_DOMAIN}). Do NOT omit or substitute audience when testing unrelated invariants, or failures will reflect documented audience requirements rather than the target invariant.

For JWT assertions used either as authorization grants or private_key_jwt client authentication, iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour. Use {{now_epoch}} for baseline assertions and vary only the target claim under test. Otherwise rejections may be caused by stale iat rather than issuer/signature/authorization behavior.

For OIDC authorization-code tests, redirect_uri at /oauth/v2/token MUST exactly match the redirect_uri used at /oauth/v2/authorize. A mismatch is documented to produce invalid_grant-style failure; do not interpret that as a session-binding or identity bug unless the same request is evaluated inconsistently.

For PKCE-based authorization-code flows, ZITADEL supports only code_challenge_method=S256. The token request MUST send the original plaintext code_verifier and the authorize request MUST send the matching code_challenge. Do not use other PKCE methods when testing I3 flow coherence.

For implicit-flow or id_token validation tests, nonce is mandatory for implicit flow and recommended generally. The fuzzer MUST send a nonce in authorize requests whenever it expects an id_token and MUST verify nonce-bound behavior separately from access-token behavior. Missing nonce can cause by-design rejection or weaken replay conclusions.

For token exchange tests, audience requested in the exchange MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject_token and actor_token. If the fuzzer requests an unrelated audience, rejection is by design and MUST NOT be reported as an authorization-binding bug.

For token exchange scope-escalation tests, invalid_scope is by design when the requested scope exceeds the scope granted by the resource owner. The oracle should treat rejection as correct behavior and only flag success if the exchanged token contains claims or scopes beyond upstream authorization.

For token exchange token-type tests, only documented token type combinations are valid. In particular, subject_token_type=refresh_token is not allowed; subject_token_type=jwt is allowed only with actor_token; requested_token_type defaults to access token if omitted. Invalid combinations must not be treated as security findings.

For introspection-based verification, active=true is returned only when the token is active AND the requesting client is part of the token audience. The fuzzer MUST introspect with the correct client context; otherwise active=false may reflect audience mismatch of the introspecting client, not token invalidity.

For userinfo-based verification, the fuzzer MUST use a user access_token, not a client-credentials token. ZITADEL explicitly documents that /oidc/v1/userinfo requires the access_token of the user, so failures with machine/client tokens are by design.

For reserved-scope audience tests, ZITADEL adds audiences through scopes such as urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:{projectid}:aud and urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:zitadel:aud. When testing audience binding, the fuzzer MUST account for these scope-driven audience expansions; otherwise extra aud values may be by design rather than over-authorization.

For organization-binding tests, requesting scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} or urn:zitadel:iam:org:domain:primary:{domainname} enforces organization membership by design. The fuzzer MUST avoid these scopes in cross-identity or cross-org baseline tests unless organization enforcement is the property under test.

For JWT IdP upstream-federation tests, ZITADEL documents validation of signature via keys endpoint, issuer match, and expiration. The fuzzer MUST preserve all original query parameters when simulating the JWT endpoint proxy and MUST deliver the JWT in the configured HTTP header, not as a URL parameter, or the OIDC flow state will break for non-security reasons.

For JWT IdP trust-anchor rotation or issuer-change tests, the valid baseline must use the configured keys endpoint and issuer, then re-run after changing trust material or issuer. ZITADEL treats the upstream JWT as an external ID token and documents issuer/signature/exp checks; failures after reconfiguration are expected and should be used as the coherence oracle.

For OIDC RP validation tests against external OIDC providers, the fuzzer SHOULD test aud, iss, exp, and nonce handling because ZITADEL acts as a relying party for external IdPs. In particular, cross-provider login tests must ensure the upstream id_token audience matches the configured client_id for that provider; otherwise rejection is correct per OIDC validation expectations.

For claims-based authorization observations, many claims are scope-gated. UserInfo and introspection only return claims 'when requested' for scopes like profile, email, phone, address, metadata, and roles. The fuzzer MUST request the relevant scopes before concluding a claim is missing or unexpectedly present.

For metadata-claim tests, urn:zitadel:iam:user:metadata values are base64 encoded by design. The oracle MUST decode or compare against base64 form; raw-value mismatches are not identity or authorization bugs.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests against login_with_jwt, the JWT bearer assertion MUST include time claims relative to the current clock: use exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} and iat={{now_epoch}} for the control token, then vary exp/nbf on the attack token. Without a valid control login, a token-endpoint failure cannot be distinguished from broken client authentication or malformed assertion setup.

JWT bearer assertions used with login_with_jwt MUST be signed with a downloaded ZITADEL service-account key and include a kid header equal to the keyId. For I1 resign_attacker_key and kid_injection tests, keep the same structural requirements (iss/sub/aud/iat/exp and kid present) and vary only the trust/signing material under test; otherwise failures may be caused by malformed client authentication rather than signature verification behavior.

For login_with_jwt, the JWT assertion aud claim MUST include ZITADEL's issuing domain as a string or array member. Do NOT use audience-mismatch attack values in aud for tests that are meant to exercise other invariants, because ZITADEL documents this as a required structural property of the JWT profile grant and the request will fail before other checks are reached.

For login_with_jwt, the JWT assertion iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour. Use iat={{now_epoch}} for control tokens. When testing exp or nbf freshness behavior, do NOT also set iat older than {{now_epoch_minus_3600}} or the request may fail for the documented iat-age rule instead of the freshness condition under test.

For exchange_code_for_token in PKCE flows, code_challenge_method supports only S256. Do NOT attempt PKCE method-variation tests using plain or other algorithms; failures are by design because ZITADEL documents S256 as the only supported algorithm.

For I3 redirect_uri_mismatch tests, exchange_code_for_token MUST first establish a control where the token request uses the exact same redirect_uri as the authorization request. ZITADEL requires an exact redirect_uri match and documents invalid_grant when the code does not match the original redirect URI; this is expected behavior, not an identity-binding issue.

For start_oidc_auth, state is only highly recommended, not mandatory. A valid I3 state_swap test MUST include state explicitly in both control and attack requests; if omitted, there is no session-binding signal to swap and any result is uninterpretable.

For start_oidc_auth implicit-flow requests, nonce MUST be provided. For code-flow requests, ZITADEL recommends nonce and returns it in the ID token when provided. For I2 replay-oriented OIDC tests, always include nonce in the control and attack authorization requests so replay resistance is actually exercised rather than skipped by configuration.

For token_exchange audience-binding tests, the requested audience parameter MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from both subject and actor tokens. If the requested audience is outside that subset, rejection is by documented design and must not be reported as a novel authorization bug.

For token_exchange wrong-audience and ignore-audience tests, first obtain a control subject_token whose aud already contains the target audience. ZITADEL documents audience as subset-constrained during token exchange, so a failing attack with an out-of-subset audience is expected and does not prove whether subject_token audience validation is correctly enforced beyond the documented subset rule.

For token_exchange scope-escalation tests, requested scope on refresh and token exchange MUST be interpreted relative to prior grants: refresh_token scope must be a subset of the original authorization request, and token exchange may return scopes that differ from the provided scope parameter. Always compare the exchanged token's actual returned scope/claims against the upstream token and requested scope, not just request acceptance.

For token_exchange type tests, only the documented token-type matrix is valid: subject_token_type refresh_token is not allowed; subject_token_type jwt is allowed only with actor_token; requested_token_type defaults to access token if omitted. Do NOT treat rejection of unsupported type combinations as a security finding.

For introspect_token, active=true additionally requires that the requesting client is part of the token audience. Therefore, a false/negative introspection result can be caused by client-audience mismatch rather than token invalidity or revocation. Use a control introspection from an audience-authorized client before drawing I1/I2 conclusions.

For revoke_session, the revocation endpoint revokes only tokens that the client has been granted. A failed or ineffective revocation attempt from the wrong client context is not evidence of replay weakness. Use the same client context that obtained the token, then verify revocation via introspect_token active=false or userinfo failure.

For verify_granted_identity, UserInfo requires an access_token of the user, not a client-only token. Do NOT use client_credentials tokens or machine-only tokens as session tokens for identity verification; resulting failures are by design and do not indicate identity confusion.

For I5 claim-presence tests using verify_granted_identity or introspect_token, many claims are scope-gated in ZITADEL. Missing email/profile/phone/address/metadata/resource-owner claims without the corresponding scopes is expected. Always request the relevant scopes in the control and attack sequences before asserting claim omission or escalation.

For I5 audience tests on access tokens, ZITADEL documents that by default all client IDs and the project ID are included in aud, and additional project audiences can be requested via reserved scopes. Do NOT assume a single-valued audience baseline; compare against the documented multi-audience behavior when evaluating overbroad audience findings.

For start_oidc_auth and exchange_code_for_token, client authentication method changes the required token request parameters: client_secret_basic uses Authorization header, PKCE uses client_id plus code_verifier, and private_key_jwt uses client_assertion plus client_assertion_type. A valid I3 coherence test must keep the client auth method constant between control and attack unless that method itself is the subject under test.

For OIDC RP-style tests involving external IdPs or JWT IdP preselection, preserve all original query parameters when redirecting/proxying to ZITADEL. The JWT IdP guide explicitly requires forwarding all original query parameters intact to preserve OIDC flow state; losing them can break state/nonce/session binding and create false I3 results.

For JWT IdP-related OIDC login tests, the upstream JWT must be delivered in an HTTP header, never as a URL parameter. If a test injects the JWT via query string and ZITADEL rejects it, that is expected per documentation and not evidence about proof validation strength.

For JWT IdP upstream validation tests, ZITADEL documents verification of signature via keys endpoint, issuer match, and expiry. A valid I1/I2 test must vary one of these checks at a time while keeping the others correct; otherwise a rejection cannot be attributed to the intended validation step.

For reserved-scope authorization tests, scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} enforces that the user is a member of the selected organization, and unknown organization IDs cause failure. Do NOT use this scope in generic control logins unless organization membership is intentionally part of the test, or you may create false I5 denials unrelated to the target invariant.

For reserved-scope authorization tests, scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:domain:primary:{domainname} enforces both organization membership and that the username is suffixed by the provided domain. This is exact value semantics from the scope string itself, not a wildcard-capable matcher. For multi-identity I4 scenarios, OMIT this scope unless every tested identity is intentionally constrained to the same exact domain suffix.

For reserved-scope audience expansion tests, scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:{projectid}:aud adds the requested project ID to the access-token audience, and urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:zitadel:aud adds the ZITADEL project ID. If these scopes are present, extra audience values are by design and must not be flagged as audience escalation.

For I2 freshness tests on login_with_jwt, the JWT profile assertion MUST include exp in the future and iat no older than 1 hour. Use template values such as iat={{now_epoch}} and exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} for control tokens. Assertions with older iat are rejected by design.

For I1 proof-integrity tests on login_with_jwt, the JWT assertion header MUST include kid matching the downloaded keyId. ZITADEL uses kid to identify the verification key; missing or wrong kid causes rejection unrelated to the intended attack.

For I1 issuer/audience validation tests on login_with_jwt, the JWT profile assertion aud MUST include ZITADEL's issuing domain (https://${CUSTOM_DOMAIN} / issuer domain). If aud does not include the issuer domain, rejection is expected and does not prove any deeper validation behavior.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests against login_with_jwt, the sequence MUST include a CONTROL login using a valid assertion (for example iat={{now_epoch}}, exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}}). Without a control, token-endpoint failure cannot be distinguished from broken client authentication or malformed assertion construction.

For I3 redirect_uri_mismatch tests on exchange_code_for_token, redirect_uri at the token endpoint MUST exactly match the redirect_uri used in start_oidc_auth. Any mismatch yields invalid_grant by design.

For I3 PKCE tests, when start_oidc_auth sends code_challenge and code_challenge_method=S256, exchange_code_for_token MUST send the matching code_verifier. ZITADEL supports only S256. Omitting code_verifier or using another method causes expected failure by design.

For I2 nonce/replay tests in OIDC implicit or hybrid-style authorization requests, nonce is mandatory for implicit flow and strongly recommended otherwise. Missing nonce in implicit flow causes expected rejection or unusable results; do not treat that as a vulnerability.

For I3 state-swap tests, state is only returned unmodified to the redirect_uri and is recommended for CSRF mitigation. The fuzzer must compare the returned state to the sent state itself; the token endpoint does not validate state because state is a client-side binding parameter.

For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, requested scope on token_exchange MUST be a subset of the scope granted by the original authorization when using refresh-like semantics. ZITADEL documents invalid_scope when requested scope exceeds what the resource owner granted; treat such rejection as correct behavior.

For I5 token_exchange_wrong_audience and token_exchange_ignore_audience tests, audience on token_exchange MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject_token and actor_token. Rejection for a broader audience is expected and should not be flagged as a bug.

For I5 token_exchange tests, resource is currently not supported. The fuzzer MUST NOT rely on resource to constrain or distinguish outcomes because unsupported resource values can cause invalid_request unrelated to audience or scope binding.

For I5 token_exchange token-type tests, ZITADEL supports only the documented token type matrix: subject_token_type access_token or id_token are allowed in specific combinations; refresh_token is not allowed; jwt as subject_token is only allowed with actor_token; requested_token_type defaults to access token if omitted. Use only documented combinations or failures are by design.

For introspect_token tests, the requesting client must be authenticated and must be part of the token audience for active=true. If the client is not in the audience, introspection may return active=false or 401 invalid_client by design; do not misclassify this as token invalidity.

For revoke_session and introspect_token, client authentication method matters. ZITADEL supports client_secret_basic and private_key_jwt for token/introspection-style endpoints. The fuzzer must keep the authentication method consistent with the registered client or failures are expected.

For I5 audience tests on access tokens, ZITADEL by default includes all client IDs and the project ID in aud, and additional audiences can be requested via reserved scopes such as urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:{projectid}:aud. Do not assume a single-valued audience; assertions about overbroad audience must account for these documented defaults and requested scopes.
For I5 metadata claim tests, urn:zitadel:iam:user:metadata values are base64 encoded. The fuzzer must decode before semantic comparison; raw encoded values are expected and not a type-confusion bug.

For I5 organization-binding tests, requesting scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} or urn:zitadel:iam:org:domain:primary:{domainname} enforces organization membership. Failures when the user is not a member are expected and should be used as controls, not flagged as authorization bugs.

For I1/I5 cross-provider JWT audience tests, when ZITADEL acts as an RP to external IdPs, the docs indicate provider-specific scopes and issuer configuration but do not document disabling aud/iss checks. The fuzzer SHOULD explicitly test cross-provider audience confusion by reusing an upstream token across providers, but must interpret failures caused by provider-specific client registration or callback mismatch as setup issues, not security passes.

For I2 replay_same_token on login_with_jwt, do NOT flag successful reuse of the same JWT profile assertion as a vulnerability unless the docs explicitly promise one-time assertion tracking. The provided documentation describes stateless JWT validation requirements (signature, issuer, expiry) but does not document jti replay prevention for JWT profile grants.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: Zitadel management API uses REST gateway paths under /management/v1/ (org-scoped). Do NOT use gRPC Connect paths (e.g., 'zitadel.idp.v2.IdentityProviderService/...'). For IdP setup: create_provider creates the IdP, enable_auth_method adds it to the login policy. Both are needed before IdP login works.
